scenes.title: Check the intended saved planned deployment

captions.text: Open the saved community support status exercise and check its incident reference.
Its badge reads Planned, and its finance mode is Operational only.
This separate fictional deployment has no rostered resources,
time reports or expenses.
Keeping it separate makes each status result easy to verify without changing
the earlier training deployment.
The badge on the left shows the stored operational state; the dropdown in
Summary prepares a possible next change.
In Summary, choose Standby and select Change status.
Confirm the change when prompted.
Before saving, the dropdown can say Standby while the deployment
badge still says Planned.
After the page returns, verify Saved and the Standby badge.
This difference is important when a supervisor checks whether an assignment is
ready or merely has an unsaved selection.
Use the saved badge as the readback of the operation you just performed.
For the next stage, choose Active in the same dropdown and select Change status.
Confirm the intended transition, then read the returned badge.
It now says Active.
The dropdown may already display the next available choice after a save, so read
it separately from the current badge.
This exercise changes the deployment’s operational stage; it does not dispatch a
call or automatically demonstrate changes to individual unit or personnel statuses.
When the fictional assignment is winding down, choose Demobilizing
and select Change status.
Confirm it and verify the saved Demobilizing badge.
The same page retains the deployment reference, window and notes.
Those details help you keep the status change attached
to the intended assignment.
Time-report submission, independent approval and equipment handover are
separate operations demonstrated in the other deployment lessons;
a status label does not establish that those tasks were completed.
Choose Completed and select Change status for this empty training exercise.
Confirm the transition and verify the returned Completed badge.
Compare that badge with the earlier prepared dropdown so you can distinguish
selection from a saved result.
In this completed view, the next-status dropdown and Change
status button are no longer offered.
The Summary still shows zero resources, time reports, personnel hours and
expenses for this separate exercise.

scenes.title: Find completed history with Show all

captions.text: Return to Deployments.
The current list no longer includes the completed status exercise.
Select Show all.
The completed exercise now appears with its Completed badge and
Operational only finance mode.
The other active and demobilizing training deployments remain separate rows.
Use this view when you need retained history rather than assuming that
an assignment disappeared or was deleted when it left the current list.

visual_required_labels: TRAINING ONLY - Community support status lifecycle

scenes.title: Reopen and verify the retained deployment

captions.text: Open the completed exercise from the retained list.
required_labels: TRAINING ONLY - Community support status lifecycle

captions.text: The fully loaded detail page still shows Completed, the same incident reference,
the window, contact and training notes.
Operational only is retained.
Reopening provides another check that the result persisted beyond
the page on which you changed it.
This demonstration follows the forward status sequence that was
actually available and saved; it does not demonstrate a backward
transition or a cancellation.

visual_required_labels: TRAINING ONLY - Community support status lifecycle

scenes.title: Keep operational stages useful for your department

captions.text: Use deployment stages to keep assignments understandable for your own department.
Community paramedicine and mental health teams can track a temporary
support assignment; search-and-rescue and security departments can track
an operation; wildland contractors and industrial emergency teams
can track a crew deployment.
Fire and E M S organizations can use the same controls.
Check the intended assignment, select its next stage, save, and verify
the badge and retained history.
Review time, equipment and finance through their separate workflows.
